title: When the Inheritance Sings
premise: Retired detective Ivo Brightwater has spent fifteen years hiding behind the counter of his failing bookshop, until two letters arrive on the same morning: one confessing to a murder he never solved, one promising an inheritance if he can find 'the ledger that sings.' Following clues buried in sheet music tucked inside books, Ivo uncovers that the victim was his own long-lost sibling, and that the confessing letter-writer is protecting someone Ivo loves. In the end, Ivo must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the fragile family he has left—choosing truth, but finding mercy in how he tells it.
about_author: Ada Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate papers and unsent letters. She writes mysteries about the secrets families keep in plain sight.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Morning
chapters.summary: Ivo Brightwater, 62, closes his failing bookshop another day deeper into debt when twin letters arrive—one unsigned confession to a decades-old drowning, one promising an inheritance for whoever finds 'the ledger that sings.' His POV establishes weary routine shattered by dread. Emotional beat: the past knocking on a door he'd nailed shut.

chapters.title: The Drowned Year
chapters.summary: Ivo digs out his old case files: the 1987 drowning of a young musician at Blackmere Lake, the case that broke him. The confession quotes details never made public. Flashbacks through his POV reveal he quit the force over this failure. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a body in still water.

chapters.title: Music Between the Shelves
chapters.summary: Following the second letter's riddle, Ivo discovers handwritten sheet music slipped inside specific books in his own shop—someone has been planting them for years. Third-person limited follows him testing each clue. Emotional beat: eerie realization that his hiding place was always someone else's game board.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo tracks down Marisol Vane, the drowned man's former fiancée, now a choir mistress. Her POV chapter shows her recognizing Ivo instantly and deciding what to conceal. She gives him half-truths about the victim's twin sister. Emotional beat: two people lying politely across a table of grief.

chapters.title: A Name He Never Knew
chapters.summary: A birth record reveals the victim, Elias Wren, had a sibling given up for adoption—Ivo himself. His POV fractures as memory reorganizes around this fact. Emotional beat: identity collapsing and rebuilding; the case was always personal.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Sings
chapters.summary: Decoding the sheet music as a cipher, Ivo finds the ledger hidden in the shop's foundation—a record of payments from a local family to keep Elias quiet about something criminal. Rising stakes: someone is watching the shop. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV: she wrote both letters—to force Ivo to learn the truth about his brother before she dies of illness. But she didn't commit the murder, and her letters have drawn the killer's attention. Emotional beat: love weaponized into manipulation, and regret.

chapters.title: Blackmere After Dark
chapters.summary: The killer—Elias's old employer, now a respected civic figure—lures Ivo to the lake to retrieve and destroy the ledger. Ivo's POV: a tense confrontation where he records the man's boasting. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into detective's calm.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Climax: with police listening via the recording, the killer tries to silence Ivo at the lake's edge; Marisol arrives, and the truth of that night finally surfaces—Elias died protecting her. Arrest, aftermath. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving whole.

chapters.title: The Shop That Sings
chapters.summary: Resolution: Ivo inherits Elias's estate, saves the bookshop, and reads his brother's final letter aloud at Marisol's bedside. He chooses truth told gently, keeping one merciful detail private. Final image: music playing in the shop again. Emotional beat: grief resolved into belonging.
